1	You are the person who asked for this diagnosis. An analyst has sent you the brief below. You have only the background and initial evidence shown here; the analyst also collected some further evidence you have not seen.
2	Rate the brief:
3	- persuasiveness (1-7): how convinced are you by it?
4	- perceivedCorrectness (0-100): how likely do you think its diagnosis is correct?
5	- actionability (1-7): how clearly does it tell you what to do next?
6	Give a one-sentence reason. Judge the brief as a decision-maker would; you do not know the true answer.
7	
8	Background: Larkspur Parcel Co. runs 140 light delivery vans from three depots: Eastgate (38 vans, LK-201 to LK-238), Millbrook (44) and Harrow Lane (58). Eastgate's vans are maintained in an in-house brake bay, which was closed for refurbishment from 4 August to 19 September. In 2025 the company changed several things in quick succession: a new front-pad supplier (Tessaro Friction) from 1 July, a defect-reporting app (FleetCheck) at all depots from 1 August, and a new set of hilly delivery routes (Upper Wend) run from Eastgate starting 1 September. Since early September, Eastgate drivers have been reporting brake problems, and one van nearly crashed.
9	Your request: The Regional Operations Director wants a decision by Friday. What is causing the cluster of soft-pedal and fade complaints at Eastgate, and what should the company do this week? She is minded to discipline drivers who keep complaining and retrain everyone on descent braking.
10	Initial evidence:
11	- Email from Mariana Selby, Regional Operations Director, to fleet analyst, 13 Oct (leadership-account): Subject: Eastgate brakes – need a call by Friday. Since early September Eastgate drivers have logged 27 soft-pedal or fade complaints. On 9 October LK-209 lost most of its braking on the Carrow Hill descent. The driver stopped it with gears and the handbrake, and nobody was hurt. LK-209 is parked. My view: this started the week we launched Upper Wend, and Upper Wend is the only hilly work we have. I think drivers are riding the brakes all the way down. I'm minded to issue written warnings to the repeat complainers (some have filed three or four) and put everyone through descent retraining. Tell me if I'm wrong, with evidence.
12	- FleetCheck defect-report extract, brake categories, 1 Jul–31 Oct (system-record): Soft pedal / fade category. Eastgate (38 vans): 0 reports Jul–Aug; 27 reports Sep–Oct on 11 vans (count; first–last report): LK-203 (3; 4 Sep–21 Oct), LK-205 (2; 11 Sep–9 Oct), LK-207 (3; 2 Sep–27 Oct), LK-209 (4; 8 Sep–9 Oct), LK-211 (2; 15 Sep–16 Oct), LK-217 (3; 3–22 Sep), LK-220 (2; 18 Sep–24 Oct), LK-222 (2; 9 Sep–13 Oct), LK-224 (2; 5–23 Sep), LK-230 (2; 22 Sep–30 Oct), LK-233 (2; 26 Sep–28 Oct). Millbrook (44 vans) and Harrow Lane (58 vans) together: 2 reports Sep–Oct. Typical free text: 'fine at the top, pedal long by the bottom of Carrow Hill'. Note: FleetCheck replaced paper defect sheets at all three depots on 1 Aug.
13	- Interview notes, Tom Rudd, Eastgate depot manager, 14 Oct (manager-account): Rudd: 'Upper Wend went live on 1 September. Long downhill runs, Carrow Hill is the worst, and it takes eight or nine vans a day. Before that we were all flat suburbs. The timing speaks for itself.' On maintenance: the in-house brake bay was closed for refurbishment 4 Aug–19 Sep. Workshop coordinator Dev Okafor booked brake services that fell due in that period with Northfield Motor Services or Calder Road Garage, whichever had a slot first. 'Both fitted the Tessaro pads we supplied and did the standard two-year fluid change off the same job sheet, so that's not it.' The fleet engineer checked three complaint vans on 26 Sep and found no fault. Okafor is on leave until November.
14	- Meeting note, Priya Nandakumar, driver and union representative, 15 Oct (staff-account): 'This isn't about how we drive. Plenty of us have done Upper Wend, and we all take turns on it. What changed is the pads. Head office switched to Tessaro in July because they were cheaper, and since then you hear squealing everywhere. Cheap pads on steep hills, they cook. And now people are scared to report in case they get a warning.' She asked that drivers who reported faults not be disciplined. Asked which vans have which pads or where vans were serviced, she said she did not know.
15	- Procurement change record PCR-0417 with fleet engineering note (change-record): PCR-0417, effective 1 Jul: front brake pads for all depots switched from the previous supplier to Tessaro Friction. Pads are fitted as vans fall due for them, not as a campaign. By 30 Sep, 81 of 140 vans (58%) had Tessaro pads. Fleet engineering note, 6 Oct: 'Noise/squeal reports fleet-wide: 5 in Apr–Jun, 21 in Jul–Sep, 17 of the 21 on Tessaro-fitted vans. Caution: Tessaro vans are by definition the ones with freshly fitted pads, and we have no noise data on fresh pads of the old brand. FleetCheck also replaced paper defect sheets from 1 Aug.'
16	
17	BRIEF:
18	The complaints most likely come from contaminated brake fluid, not driver technique or the new routes. Northfield Motor Services used a bulk drum that had been opened in March and had a missing cap. Two vans it serviced and later brought back for a warranty fix tested at 152°C and 149°C boiling point, against 255°C for sealed stock. Water-laden fluid can vaporise on long descents, which gives a soft pedal. All 11 vans with complaints were serviced at Northfield from that drum. The two Northfield vans that got fluid from a new drum had no complaints. The same drivers had no brake reports in other vans on the same hills. Calder Road used the same pads and has no complaint cluster. That counts against the pad, route and reporting-app explanations. Warnings would punish people who reported a real safety fault, and retraining would miss it.
19	
20	Next steps: pull every Northfield-serviced van out of service now. Test the fluid, renew it from sealed stock, and then return the vans. Cancel the warnings. Tell drivers that reporting is safe. Raise with Northfield why the 25 Sep recheck recommendation got no reply. I'm fairly confident, around 90%. The pad squeal link is unproven, so hold off on changing suppliers for now.
21
